payload.prompt: Which API calls a Foundry model deployment from code?

options.rationale: The OpenAI-compatible Responses API makes direct calls to a deployed Foundry model. It returns the model's generated output.

options.error_type: Confuses direct model calls with agent calls
options.rationale: The Project API supports connecting applications to saved agents. It is not the direct model-calling API.
options.better_fit: Use the Project API when an application must integrate and call an existing agent.

options.rationale: The Tool Catalog is used to discover and manage capabilities. It does not send requests to a model deployment.
options.better_fit: Use the Tool Catalog when centrally managing tools for agents.

options.rationale: The playground is used to test prompts and settings interactively. It is not an API used by application code.
options.better_fit: Use the playground to test a model configuration before implementing it.

payload.feedback_for_correct: Correct. The Responses API is the direct route from code to a deployed model.

payload.prompt: Which are features of a lightweight chat client? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: A lightweight chat client accepts a person's request. It sends that request to a remote service.

options.text: It calls a remote API or service
options.rationale: Calling a remote service is a core job of the client. Most compute can remain on the server.
The client presents the returned response to the user. Displaying results completes its focused interaction loop.

options.text: It requires a heavy UI framework
options.error_type: Confuses lightweight clients with complex applications
options.rationale: A lightweight client avoids heavy frameworks and large local dependencies. It can be a simple CLI, utility, or web page.
options.better_fit: A heavy framework may fit a large application with a complex interface.

payload.feedback_for_correct: Correct. A lightweight client collects input, makes a remote call, and shows the result.

payload.prompt: Is the following statement accurate?
payload.statement: A lightweight chat client must include complex backend logic and large local dependencies.
payload.feedback_for_correct: Correct. Lightweight clients intentionally avoid heavy local complexity.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: Adding that complexity would make a simple prototype harder to run.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: A lightweight client can use minimal configuration while the remote service performs most computation.

payload.prompt: Complete the description of the small application.

parts.text: A small application that collects input, calls a remote service, and displays results is a

payload.explanation: A lightweight chat client has a focused role: gather input, call a remote service, and display the result without heavy local complexity.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The term would fail to identify the small client application being described.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Use “lightweight chat client,” which describes the application rather than the API it calls.

payload.prompt: A developer is building a simple command-line tool for a marketing team. It sends a product-description request to a deployed model and prints the reply. What should the developer build?

options.text: A lightweight chat client using Responses API
options.rationale: A small command-line application can collect a request, call a deployed model, and print the reply. That is the role of a lightweight chat client using the Responses API.

options.text: An agent called through Project API
options.error_type: Confuses direct model calls with agent calls
options.rationale: The scenario only requires direct model inference. An existing packaged agent is not required.
options.better_fit: Choose this when the application must call a saved agent with reusable behavior.

feedback.intrinsic: The developer would add unnecessary saved-agent setup.
feedback.instructional: For a direct model request in a small CLI, use a lightweight client and the Responses API.

options.rationale: Benchmarking compares candidate models. It does not build the command-line application that sends requests.
options.better_fit: Use a benchmark comparison while selecting a suitable model.

feedback.intrinsic: The team would have comparison data but no working client.
feedback.instructional: The required application is a lightweight client that calls the deployment.

options.error_type: Confuses an app with tool management
options.rationale: A Tool Catalog entry manages a callable capability. It is not the client application described.
options.better_fit: Use the Tool Catalog to discover and manage tools for an agent.

feedback.intrinsic: The request would still lack an application that sends it to the model.
feedback.instructional: Build the lightweight client and call the deployment through the Responses API.

payload.feedback_for_correct: Correct. This is a direct model call in a small client application.

payload.prompt: What does the Foundry SDK provide? Select all that apply.

options.text: A Project client for Foundry operations
options.rationale: The SDK provides a Project client for Foundry-native operations. This client connects application work to a Foundry project.

options.text: An OpenAI-compatible client for model calls
options.rationale: The SDK also provides an OpenAI-compatible client. That client supports Responses API model calls.
Model evaluation scores come from Foundry's benchmarking and evaluator capabilities, not from the SDK clients. The SDK provides clients for Foundry operations and model calls.
options.better_fit: Use evaluation scores when comparing model quality, safety, or performance.

options.text: A replacement for a model deployment
options.rationale: An SDK supplies clients and connection patterns. A deployment is the model service being called.
options.better_fit: A model deployment is needed to expose a selected model through an endpoint.

payload.feedback_for_correct: Correct. The Foundry SDK provides a Project client for Foundry operations and an OpenAI-compatible client for model calls. Model evaluation scores come from Foundry evaluation features, not the SDK.

payload.prompt: Which Foundry SDK client is used for Foundry-native operations?

options.rationale: The Project client is supplied by the Foundry SDK for Foundry-native operations. It is distinct from the OpenAI-compatible model-call client.

options.error_type: Confuses model calls with Foundry operations
options.rationale: The OpenAI-compatible client is used for Responses API model calls. It does not have the Project client's stated role.
options.better_fit: Use it for direct model calls through the Responses API.

options.error_type: Confuses a request value with a client
options.rationale: agent_reference is a request value used to target an existing agent. It is not an SDK client.
options.better_fit: Use it in extra_body when directing a Responses API request to a saved agent.

options.rationale: The SDK's stated client roles are Project client and OpenAI-compatible client. The Tool Catalog is for managing capabilities.
options.better_fit: Use the Tool Catalog when discovering and managing callable tools.

payload.feedback_for_correct: Correct. The Project client handles Foundry-native operations.

payload.prompt: Evaluate this statement.
payload.statement: System prompts, user prompts, and parameter values tested in the playground can be reused in application code.
payload.feedback_for_correct: Correct. Tested prompts and settings can be carried into code.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The team would needlessly recreate a configuration that already worked.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Reuse the tested system prompts, user prompts, and parameter values in the application.

payload.prompt: Reconstruct the statement from the pieces.
payload.explanation: The Project client is for Foundry operations, while the OpenAI-compatible client is for model calls.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The clients would be paired with the wrong jobs.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Keep each client immediately beside the purpose it serves.

payload.prompt: A developer tested customer-support prompts in the playground and is moving the chat into an app. Which items should the developer reuse? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: A tested system prompt defines a working behavior configuration. Reusing it helps preserve that behavior in the application.
Tested user prompts capture effective request patterns. They can be reused in application code.
Parameter values affect generation behavior. Tested values can be carried from the playground into code.

options.error_type: Confuses evaluation results with runtime settings
options.rationale: Benchmark scores compare models but do not reproduce the working prompt configuration. The tested prompts and parameter values do.
options.better_fit: Use benchmark scores when selecting among candidate models.

feedback.intrinsic: The app could lose the configuration that made its responses work.
feedback.instructional: Reuse tested prompts and parameters to preserve the working setup.

payload.feedback_for_correct: Correct. Carry the tested prompts and parameter values into the app.

payload.prompt: What is a model when used on its own?

options.rationale: A model provides the raw intelligence used for inference. It generates output from a prompt.
A packaged, task-oriented worker is an agent built on a model. A model is the underlying intelligence.
options.better_fit: Use this description for an agent with reusable behavior.

options.rationale: External actions are supplied by tools. The model supplies reasoning and generation.
options.better_fit: Use this for callable capabilities such as search or database queries.

options.rationale: Retrieved documents are knowledge used as context. They are separate from the model that generates the response.
options.better_fit: Use this for external content that grounds an answer.

payload.feedback_for_correct: Correct. A model alone is raw intelligence for inference.

payload.prompt: Is the following statement accurate?
payload.statement: An agent is only a one-off prompt sent directly to a model.
payload.feedback_for_correct: Correct. An agent packages reusable, consistent workflow-like behavior.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: A one-off request would not ensure consistent behavior across applications.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: An agent is a reusable, task-oriented worker built on a model.

payload.prompt: Complete the definition.

parts.text: A packaged, task-oriented worker built on a model is an

payload.explanation: An agent packages a model into reusable, task-oriented behavior.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The selected term would identify only a component rather than the reusable worker.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Use “agent” for the packaged worker built on a model.

payload.prompt: Put the pieces in the correct order.
payload.explanation: The sentence identifies an agent as the worker and then states that it is built on a model.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The relationship between the worker and its underlying model would be unclear.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Name the packaged worker first, then show what it is built on.

payload.prompt: A customer-support manager needs the same assistant behavior in the company website and support bot. The assistant must follow one consistent workflow. What should the manager create?

options.rationale: An agent packages consistent workflow-like behavior for reuse across applications. That meets the website and support-bot requirement.

options.error_type: Confuses reusable workflow with one-off inference
options.rationale: A direct prompt supports a single inference request. It does not package consistent behavior for reuse.
options.better_fit: Use a direct model prompt for a one-off inference task.

feedback.intrinsic: The two experiences could drift into different behaviors.
feedback.instructional: Use an agent when a workflow must remain consistent across applications.

options.rationale: Benchmarks compare model performance. They do not define a reusable support workflow.
options.better_fit: Use benchmarks while evaluating candidate models.

feedback.intrinsic: The manager would have selection information but no shared behavior.
feedback.instructional: An agent packages how the chosen model should behave.

options.rationale: Token allocation controls capacity and rate limits. It does not create a consistent support workflow.
options.better_fit: Use token allocation when planning deployment throughput.

feedback.intrinsic: Capacity could change while the website and bot still lack shared behavior.
feedback.instructional: Choose an agent for reusable behavior across experiences.

payload.feedback_for_correct: Correct. An agent can package one workflow for both experiences.

payload.prompt: Which three parts make up a Foundry agent? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: A Foundry agent contains a model for reasoning. It is the intelligence used by the agent.
Instructions define the agent's role, style, constraints, and output rules. They guide consistent behavior.
Tools provide actions through external systems. They enable the agent to act when needed.

options.error_type: Confuses an agent component with evaluation
options.rationale: A leaderboard compares models using evaluation attributes. It is not an agent component.
options.better_fit: Use a leaderboard when comparing candidate models.

payload.feedback_for_correct: Correct. An agent combines a model, instructions, and tools.

payload.prompt: Which agent component defines role, style, constraints, and output rules?

options.rationale: Instructions define role, behavior, style, constraints, and output rules. They guide how the agent responds.
The model provides reasoning and generation. It does not itself specify behavior boundaries.
options.better_fit: Use a model for the agent's reasoning capability.

options.rationale: Tools let an agent take actions through external systems. They do not set tone or output requirements.
options.better_fit: Use tools when the agent must search, query, or act externally.

options.rationale: Knowledge supplies retrieved context. It does not define the agent's role or output style.
options.better_fit: Use knowledge to ground responses in relevant content.

payload.feedback_for_correct: Correct. Instructions define the agent's behavior.

payload.prompt: Decide whether this statement is true or false.
payload.statement: An agent can maintain working memory during a conversation and create structured outputs.
payload.feedback_for_correct: Correct. Agents can maintain working memory and create structured outputs.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The agent's multi-step conversational capabilities would be underestimated.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Agents can maintain working memory, decide actions, and create structured outputs.

payload.prompt: Arrange the parts to form the correct statement.
payload.explanation: A Foundry agent combines a model, instructions that define behavior, and tools that provide actions.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The components would not be clearly connected to their roles.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Build the sentence from the agent to its model, instructions, and tools.

payload.prompt: A training-platform designer is building an assistant that creates custom quizzes and study guides. The assistant must reason, follow a tutoring style, and take needed actions. Which choices help make it an agent? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: A model provides the agent's reasoning capability. It supports generating the requested learning content.

options.text: Write instructions for a helpful tutoring style
options.rationale: Instructions define role, style, constraints, and output rules. They can establish the desired tutoring style.
Tools let the agent act through external systems when needed. They are a core agent component.
Output rules are part of instructions and support consistent behavior. Removing them undermines the requested tutoring style.
options.better_fit: No stated agent-design goal requires removing output rules.

feedback.intrinsic: Learners could receive inconsistent quizzes and study guides.
feedback.instructional: Keep instructions that define tutoring style and output requirements.

payload.feedback_for_correct: Correct. Reasoning, instructions, and tools package the assistant as an agent.

payload.prompt: What is knowledge in a Foundry agent?

options.rationale: Knowledge is external content retrieved as relevant context. It grounds responses in documents, datasets, or internal sites.

options.text: An action through an external system
options.rationale: An external action is performed by a tool. Knowledge instead provides retrieved context.
options.better_fit: Use this description for a tool such as web search or a database query.

options.rationale: Behavior rules are instructions. Knowledge is retrieved external content.
options.better_fit: Use this for instructions that guide an agent's responses.

options.rationale: Safety scores come from evaluators. Knowledge provides context during response generation.
options.better_fit: Use this for an evaluator that measures output safety.

payload.feedback_for_correct: Correct. Knowledge is retrieved external context for grounding a response.

payload.prompt: Is the following statement accurate?
payload.statement: Tools are retrieved context, while knowledge is used to take actions in external systems.
payload.feedback_for_correct: Correct. The statement reverses the two roles.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The assistant could be configured for the wrong need: retrieval or action.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Tools are actions through external systems; knowledge is retrieved context.

payload.prompt: Complete the RAG purpose.

parts.text: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) retrieves external content to

payload.explanation: RAG retrieves relevant knowledge as context so that it grounds a response.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The response would lack the purpose of the retrieved context.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: RAG retrieves knowledge to ground a response, not to perform an external action.

payload.prompt: Order the pieces correctly.
payload.explanation: A tool is a callable capability that enables a model to act through an external system.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The action role of a tool would become unclear.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Place the capability first, then show that it lets the model act externally.

payload.prompt: A human-resources employee asks an assistant about an internal policy PDF. The assistant must retrieve the relevant policy text and cite its source. What should the team add?

options.rationale: Knowledge can include internal PDFs and RAG retrieves relevant content. This grounds the answer and supports citations.
Updating a system is an external action. The request instead needs policy context and a citation.
options.better_fit: Use an update tool when the assistant must change an external system.

feedback.intrinsic: The employee could trigger a change without receiving the policy information.
feedback.instructional: Use knowledge with RAG to retrieve and cite relevant PDF content.

options.rationale: A safety evaluator assesses output for issues. It does not retrieve policy text as context.
options.better_fit: Use a safety evaluator to measure responsible output concerns.

feedback.intrinsic: The answer could be scored but still lack the requested policy passage.
feedback.instructional: Use knowledge retrieval when a document must ground the answer.

options.rationale: A deployment exposes a model through an endpoint. It does not by itself retrieve or cite internal documents.
options.better_fit: Use a deployment when making a selected model available to applications.

feedback.intrinsic: The assistant could generate an answer without the required policy context.
feedback.instructional: Add knowledge and RAG for grounded, citable document answers.

payload.feedback_for_correct: Correct. Knowledge with RAG retrieves the PDF content and grounds the response.

payload.prompt: What can the Project API do for agents? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: The Project API can integrate agents into web applications. It also supports bots and backend workflows.
The Project API can orchestrate multi-step tasks. This supports workflow-oriented agent use.

options.text: Pass structured inputs or tool calls
options.rationale: The Project API can pass structured inputs or tool calls. This supports application-driven agent workflows.

options.error_type: Confuses calling an agent with defining behavior
options.rationale: Instructions are part of the agent and define its behavior. The Project API connects an application to that agent.
options.better_fit: Use agent instructions when creating or refining the agent's behavior.

payload.feedback_for_correct: Correct. The Project API integrates agents and supports workflow operations.

payload.prompt: Evaluate this statement.
payload.statement: An agent ID identifies an agent for programmatic use, and it is available in the agent Playground code view environment variables.
payload.feedback_for_correct: Correct. The agent ID identifies the saved agent for an application call.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The client would lack the identifier needed to target the existing agent.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: The agent Playground code view provides the agent ID in its environment variables.

payload.prompt: Arrange the following steps for calling an existing agent.
payload.explanation: Authenticate the project client, retrieve the agent, obtain an OpenAI client, target the agent with agent_reference, and then print the output.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The request could be prepared before the client identifies the agent.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Authenticate first, identify the saved agent, then direct the request and read its output.

payload.prompt: Complete the request pattern.

parts.text: In a Responses API request, use
in extra_body to direct the call to an existing agent.

payload.explanation: agent_reference is the request value that targets an existing agent.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The request would not clearly target the saved agent.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Use agent_reference in extra_body; credentials and output fields serve different roles.

payload.prompt: A customer-support developer is adding an existing Foundry agent to the company support bot. The bot must send requests to that saved agent. Which steps belong in the client application? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: AIProjectClient connects the application to the Foundry project. It is authenticated in the stated client pattern.
Retrieving the agent identifies the saved worker to use. It prepares the application to target that agent.
agent_reference directs the Responses API request to the existing agent. It is included in extra_body.

options.text: Use only a model deployment name
options.error_type: Confuses direct model calls with agent calls
options.rationale: A deployment name alone is used for direct model calls. Calling a saved agent requires the project pattern and agent_reference.
options.better_fit: Use only a deployment name for a direct model call without an existing agent.

feedback.intrinsic: The bot would bypass the saved agent and its packaged behavior.
feedback.instructional: Connect to the project, retrieve the agent, and target it with agent_reference.

payload.feedback_for_correct: Correct. These steps connect the application and direct requests to the existing agent.

flashcards.back: The OpenAI-compatible Responses API calls a Foundry model deployment.

flashcards.front: What does the Foundry SDK provide?
flashcards.back: It provides Project and OpenAI-compatible clients.
An agent is a packaged, task-oriented worker built on a model.
Tools are actions; knowledge is retrieved context.
